# Getting started

Start an app with npm create protobase, install the repository, run the ERP, real estate and property portal examples and learn the development commands.

Protobase is a config-driven admin panel framework for existing Postgres databases. Data config lives in `data.ts`, UI config in `ui.ts`; a Hono server serves the API and a React app renders the admin. Coding agents get the guides and reference of the installed version with [`protobase skill install`](reference/cli.md#skill).

An app's own React code, its components, field types and actions, is a [plugin](reference/plugins.md): built on its own against a plugin API that Protobase's releases keep, and loaded by the admin app when it starts. Protobase maintains the admin app, the API and the server, and a plugin keeps working as the app moves to newer releases, with their fixes and features, without changes of its own. Below 1.0 a new minor version may still change the config, and the bundle is built again for it; the plugins' code stays as it is (see [Who maintains what](reference/plugins.md#who-maintains-what)).

## Start an app

`npm create protobase my-app` asks which preset to start from, scratch (the default), the ERP or real estate, writes the project into `my-app`, with the `@protobase` packages in the range of the latest release's major, and prints the next steps: install it with Bun, point `.env` at a Postgres database, migrate it, load the preset's base data, if it has any, create a user and run `bun run dev`. `--preset <name>` picks one without asking; without a terminal it takes scratch. It needs Node 22.12 or later. Each preset has an `AGENTS.md` with the rules for a coding agent that changes the app, such as a new migration file for every schema change.

```sh
npm create protobase my-app
npm create protobase my-app -- --preset real-estate
```

## Admin over an existing database

For a Postgres database you already have, [Admin over an existing database](guides/existing-database.md) goes from an empty folder to signing in: install the packages, scaffold the config from the tables, check it with `doctor`, add sign-in and its tables, create the first admin and run `protobase dev`.

## Docs as Markdown

Every page of these docs is also Markdown at its address plus `.md`: `https://docs.protobase.net/reference/cli/` is also `https://docs.protobase.net/reference/cli.md`. The code a page shows from example files is written out in it, and its live demos are left out, so a coding agent or a chat assistant reads the page whole. In a project, [`protobase skill install`](reference/cli.md#skill) gives coding agents the docs of the installed version.

The rest of this page works in a clone of this repository, on its examples.

## Setup

Requires Bun 1.4.2, which installs the repository and runs its scripts and tests, and Node 22.12 or later (`.nvmrc`) for the smoke test on Node.

```sh
bun install
```

## Run the ERP example

`examples/erp` is a sample ERP on a real Postgres database, seeded with three years of history. It needs Docker for the database: `bun run db:up` starts the Postgres container and gives each example its database and a `.env` from its `.env.example`.

```sh
bun run db:up && bun run --cwd examples/erp db:migrate && bun run --cwd examples/erp db:seed --scale small   # the ERP's tables and Better Auth's
bun run --cwd examples/erp protobase users create you@example.com --generate-password
bun run --cwd examples/erp dev                          # http://localhost:5173
```

`BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` in `examples/erp/.env` signs the session cookies; see [Login with Better Auth](reference/auth.md). `protobase dev` serves the admin app and the API on one port and reloads both on every change ([CLI](reference/cli.md#dev)). Its startup message says how to sign in: while the database has no users, it prints the exact `users create` command for the first admin. It stops with a clear message when another server holds its port; pass `--port 5174` to run a second app beside it.

## Run the real estate example

`examples/real-estate` is a rental and property management firm: owners, properties and units, leases and tenants, monthly rent, payments and arrears, and maintenance. Its database sits beside the ERP's in the same Postgres container, and it keeps its own `.env`.

```sh
bun run db:up && bun run --cwd examples/real-estate db:migrate && bun run --cwd examples/real-estate db:seed --scale small
bun run --cwd examples/real-estate protobase users create you@example.com --role admin --generate-password
bun run --cwd examples/real-estate dev                  # http://localhost:5173
```

## Run the property portal example

`examples/property-portal` is a public portal of homes for sale and for rent in the Netherlands and Spain. Visitors browse and filter the listings without signing in, through the [anonymous role](reference/access.md#anonymous-access); members save searches of the listings that mail them new homes, and keep favorites and notes that only they see. The seed makes two members, `anna@portal.example` and `bram@portal.example`, and an admin, `admin@portal.example`, all with the password `property-portal-demo`.

```sh
bun run db:up && bun run --cwd examples/property-portal db:migrate && bun run --cwd examples/property-portal db:seed --scale small
bun run --cwd examples/property-portal dev              # http://localhost:5173
```

## Commands

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `bun run db:up` / `bun run db:down` | start or stop the Postgres container; `db:up` also creates the examples' databases and `.env` files |
| `bun run test` | the unit tests and the snapshot tests in `packages/*/tests/` and `tests/` (Vitest projects `unit*` and `snapshot*`): no Postgres server, subprocess or network. A snapshot test replays the SQL recorded for it from Postgres in `<test>.sql.json` |
| `bun run test:record` | runs the snapshot tests on the Postgres container instead and writes their recordings, after building their templates (`bun run test:db snapshots`); run it when a change makes a snapshot test fail with `stale snapshot` |
| `bun run test:unit` | only the unit tests, next to the code (Vitest projects `unit`, whose files share their modules, and `unit-isolated`, for those that mock a module or change a global), fully parallel; starting a Postgres client there throws |
| `bun run test:watch` | `bun run test` in watch mode |
| `bun run test:integration` | the database, subprocess and build tests (projects `integration*`), against the Postgres container, among them the real-Postgres tests (`*.postgres.test.ts`) |
| `bun run test:smoke` / `node --run test:smoke` | the CLI on Bun or on Node builds the ERP and serves its bundle, whose `€` must come back intact; part of `test:integration` on Bun |
| `bun run presets:write <version> <dir>` | writes each preset to `<dir>/<name>`: a standalone copy of its example with the `@protobase` packages in the range of `<version>`'s major (`>=0.y.z <1` below 1.0, `^x.y.z` from 1.0) and its own `bun.lock` at exactly `<version>`, which must be on npm |
| `bun run images:context` | the build contexts of the `protobase` and `protobase-dev` images in `dist/images`, at the version in `package.json` (see [Deploy](guides/deploy.md#images)) |
| `bun run test:presets` | writes each preset as `bun run presets:write` does it and installs it with Bun from npm (so at a published version), then migrates, seeds, checks, tests and builds it on a database of its own, as a role without superuser rights; needs the Postgres container |
| `bun run test:postgres` | the Postgres suite in `tests/postgres/` (Vitest project `postgres`): the ERP's medium seed and the planner's statistics on it, and the jobs and event delivery through PgBouncer; needs the Postgres and PgBouncer containers and `bun run test:db postgres` |
| `bun run test:db` | builds the template databases the database tests clone for each run (`protobase_test_template`, `real_estate_test_template`, `property_portal_test_template`, all at small scale, and the empty, auth and jobs `snapshot_*_test_template` the real-Postgres and end-to-end tests clone), when missing or older than what they are built from; without them those tests skip. `bun run test:db postgres` builds the Postgres suite's (`protobase_medium_test_template`, the ERP at medium scale), `bun run test:db snapshots` the ones `test:record` records on (`snapshot_*_test_template`). Tests never use the `protobase`, `real_estate` or `property_portal` databases |
| `bun run typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` |
| `bun run check:boundaries` | dependency-cruiser package rules |
| `bun run check` | typecheck + test + test:integration + check:boundaries |
| `bun run storybook` | Storybook on port 6006 |
| `bun run build-storybook` | static Storybook build; its toolbar switches every story between light and dark |
| `bun run screenshots` / `bun run screenshots:dark` | screenshots of the stories tagged `website`, in light into `screenshots/`, in dark into `screenshots/dark/` |
| `bun run build:serve` | the serve runtime, `dist/protobase-serve.js` (see [Deploy](guides/deploy.md)) |
| `bun run docs:dev` | this site on port 4321 |
| `bun run docs:build` | this site, built into `website/dist/`; fails on broken links |
| `bun run release --dry-run` | the next version and its changelog, from the commits since the last release (see [Versioning](reference/versioning.md)) |
| `bun run docs:check` | opens every page of the built site in Chromium and fails on console errors and failed requests; `BASE=https://docs.protobase.net` checks the live site |

Each public import is a package in `packages/` (`@protobase/schema`, `layout`, `query`, `client`, `ui`, `server`, and `cli` for the `protobase` command); `packages/presets` writes the projects a new app starts from and is not published; `packages/create-protobase` is `npm create protobase`, with every preset. See [Architecture](reference/architecture.md) for the layout and import rules.
